Maria K.: quick heads-up — I found a correctness regression when activation quantization + mixed-precision matmul are enabled (FP8 path).
Ken L.: ugh, when did this land? any CL/commit id?
Maria K.: looks like it showed up after the runtime kernel-selection change last night. suspecting the FP8 activation pack/unpack around matmul. commit `3b9c7f4` in runtime/kernel-selector.
Devon R.: can you repro deterministically? small test case?
Maria K.: yes — minimal repro attached below (reproduces on nightly with our internal GPT-2-ish model). Outputs diverge ~step 2 after kv cache starts being reused.
Maria K.: ```python
# repro (simplified)
model = load_model('gpt-small', quantize_activations=True, matmul_mode='mixed_fp8_fp16')
ctx = model.new_context()
out1 = model.generate(ctx, "The weather is")
# compare with fp16-only
model2 = load_model('gpt-small', quantize_activations=False, matmul_mode='fp16')
out2 = model2.generate(ctx, "The weather is")
print(diff_tokens(out1, out2))
```
Priya S.: interesting that KV reuse correlates. could be a scale/offset applied incorrectly when storing activations in FP8.
Ken L.: I profiled kernel timeline with perf-bot, see spike at `mixed_matmul_fp8` and then a later memcpy when writing KV.
perf-bot: profiling: 1765239901 - attached flamegraph url: https://ci.redwood/infer/profiles/1765239901 (summary: mixed_matmul_fp8 42% wall, kv_write memcpy 12%).
Devon R.: does the FP8 dequant/quant path use the same calibration params for matmul and KV pack? we had a split earlier and that caused a subtle mismatch.
Maria K.: good call — I dug into the serialization: matmul uses per-tile scale from `select_kernel()` but kv_cache write uses global activation_scale from `quantization_state` if available; when we pick fp8 kernel dynamically the per-tile scale wasn't being copied over.
Priya S.: that would create tiny rounding bias that accumulates on autoregressive sampling.
Ken L.: mitigation idea: make kernel selection return a canonical QuantParams struct and thread it to all downstream packers + KV writer. simple patch.
Devon R.: before we patch, can we add an assert/regression test? maybe check a deterministically seeded 32-token generation matches FP16 baseline within n token edits.
Maria K.: added a unit test locally that fails consistently. pushing a small PR with test + fix. CL: `mr/flow/621-activation-fp8-kv-fix` (WIP).
Priya S.: any perf impact from copying QuantParams? hope it's negligible.
Ken L.: microbenchmarks: adding a 32-byte copy per tile is <0.2% on p3.8x — acceptable for correctness.
Devon R.: also noticed our batching heuristics mask small batches into larger groupings; if kernel pick is lazy-per-batch we might end up using inconsistent params across requests in a micro-batch. we should ensure quant params are resolved per-request before batch aggregation.
Maria K.: yep — current impl resolves on first matmul invocation which can be after batching. I'll move resolution to pre-batch hook.
perf-bot: regression check: running nightly perf harness on candidate MR shows throughput +0.5% and latency +0.8ms (95p) for fp8 workloads. link: https://ci.redwood/infer/regressions/621
Ken L.: good. once PR is up, let's run full evaluation: 1) accuracy eval on prompts, 2) perf benchmark with varying batch sizes and seq lengths, 3) KV stress test.
Priya S.: for accuracy eval, calibrate with and without calibration step — calibration can influence FP8 dynamic range. this could mask/fix errors; we need to ensure deterministic calibration seed.
Devon R.: note: calibration uses sample statistics from a random subset — add fixed seed to avoid CI flakiness.
Maria K.: PR uploaded: https://git.redwood/runtime/-/merge_requests/621 — I included: fix to propagate QuantParams, pre-batch resolution, unit test, and a reproducible calibration flag.
Ken L.: reviewing now. quick nit: rename `quant_state->active_scale` to `resolved_quant_params` for clarity.
Maria K.: will update. thanks.
Devon R.: heads-up for eng-ml: if you rely on activation-quantized checkpoints, you might want to re-run calibration after this change.
Priya S.: dropping a note to #eng-ml.
perf-bot: deploy-bot: staging rollout started for runtime:mr-621 at 1765240200
Maria K.: rolling to staging to validate against internal eval set. will post results in ~15m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Ken L.: awesome, thanks for catching this. small change but high impact. :tada:
